meta.title: PWA update plan - refinement proposals collected from other components
meta.status_note: Proposal only. Collected from the Admin Console plan (on hold after AC9); to be converted into a comprehensive PWA plan later. Nothing here is scheduled or built. 2026-11-16: the owner scheduled a PWA refinement round for these items and the backend follow-ups (meta.pending_intake_from_backend). 2026-11-16 (backend S25b): the backend follow-ups are items PB-01..PB-08; nothing is scheduled or built yet. 2026-11-16 (after the backend closure): PB-09 added for the monthly odometer prompt (owner answer to DQ-24; backend S26b.T1). Later on 2026-11-16: PB-10 (Neshan basemap, supersedes R-24) and PB-11 (phone sign-in while SMS is a mock, DQ-28) added; backend task ids follow the S26a/S26b/S26c split.
meta.format: Machine-readable. raw_text is the source recommendation verbatim; proposal is a first, unreviewed suggestion.
decisions_from_owner_2026_11_12: No part of backend, admin console or PWA goes to a test run until the whole plan is complete (PD-03). Test-related items below therefore wait for the full test run.
The business web app (cp-web-portal) starts at AC11 (OQ-09), which triggers the shared-package extraction.
decisions_from_owner_2026_11_16: The PWA goes through another round of refinement that implements the recommendations from the admin console development and the backend development (owner, 2026-11-16, Notice 2).

Backend S25b.T7 (2026-11-16) turned the backend and admin console follow-ups into items PB-01..PB-08 for the PWA refinement round; with R-01, R-10, R-11, R-12, R-13 and R-24 they are the round's intake.

items.raw_text: When the business web app (cp-web-portal) starts, extract the BFF core (session, oauth, dpop, private_key_jwt, forwarder, csrf), the typed client and the design-system kit from pwa/ and frontend/admin-console/ into shared packages instead of making a third copy.
items.proposal: Extract the framework-free BFF core out of pwa/src/server/bff (session store port, oauth client, dpop, private_key_jwt signer, forwarder with registry allowlist, csrf, http/header hygiene, auth-proxy, redis), the typed client (src/lib/api) and the ported design-system kit (src/components/ds) into shared packages under shared/, consumed by pwa, admin-console and cp-web-portal. Keep per-app config, session lifetimes, cookies, callback checks and allowlist source outside the shared core.
known_pwa_context: The admin console copy carries provenance headers that point back to these files.
open_questions: Package manager layout: shared/ is not a pnpm workspace today (each app has its own lockfile, GD-01 of the console).
Versioning and release of the shared packages.
Order: extract from pwa first, or from the console (which has the aal3 and purpose/reason additions)?

items.raw_text: At the next PWA stage run its pnpm test:int and pnpm e2e once against the backend at contract 1.3.0 (AC2 changed only generated types, three version strings and one template list in pwa/, checked by its unit tests, lint and contract:check).
items.trigger: full test run (after the whole plan is complete)
items.proposal: Run pnpm test:int and pnpm e2e once against the strict backend at the newest contract version (1.4.0 or later, after the backend refinement), and fix whatever the contract changes since 1.2.0/1.3.0 broke. After 1.3.0 the PWA was only checked by unit tests, lint and contract:check.
known_pwa_context: pwa/package.json: test:int = vitest run --project integration; e2e = pnpm build && playwright test

items.raw_text: Put the integration-test settings of README "Integration tests" into backend/.env (or a small script) so pnpm test:int of the console and of the PWA run against one strict backend without hand-set variables; the console test creates one ADM account per run in the dev database (bff-int-…@staff.carpals.test), harmless but visible in `pnpm dev:staff list`.
items.proposal: Define one source for the integration-test environment (strict auth flag, client keys, ports) so pwa and admin-console tests run against one strict backend without hand-set variables: either documented keys in backend/.env (with backend/.env.example entries) or a small script that exports them. The PWA side needs its test:int and e2e commands to read that source.
open_questions: Keep secrets (client private keys) in a git-ignored local file the commands source (also R-20 of the console)?
Script location: backend/tools, a root script, or per app?
related: R-04 (root script that runs both apps checks)
items.backend_part_done: backend S25b (2026-11-16): backend/tools/int-env.mjs (pnpm int:env init | backend | clients | env): one git-ignored source (backend/.env.test, backend/.env.test-clients) with strict auth and the three clients' keys; the console's test:int runs strict with one command, then dev:staff prune. The PWA half is PB-08.

items.raw_text: Three BFF copies now share most code (PWA, console, later the portal): extract them when cp-web-portal starts (R-01). The console copy differs in config, session lifetimes and cookies, the aal3/staff checks of the callback, the allowlist source and the purpose/reason headers; everything else (crypto, csrf, http, dpop, token client, redis, auth proxy) is the same.
items.proposal: Same work as R-01, seen from the BFF side: the three BFF copies differ only in config, session lifetimes and cookies, the aal3/staff checks of the callback, the allowlist source and the purpose/reason headers. Track as one extraction task with R-01; the PWA keeps its guest/anonymous token handling and cp-ssr as app-level code.

items.raw_text: PWA: check its notFound() pages in the production build (pnpm e2e on :3100). The PWA's P3 note says the not-found body is drawn on the client; under the enforced Trusted Types CSP the console found that draw blocked (blank page, D-26). If the PWA shows the same, render the not-found state in the page there too, or give the error shell a policy.
items.proposal: In the production build with the enforced Trusted Types CSP, open a not-found route and check the page is not blank. If it is, render the not-found body in the page itself (server-rendered) or give the error shell a Trusted Types policy, as the console did.
known_pwa_context: Related console deviation D-26: No-permission and not-found are states the console page renders inside the shell (status 200), not forbidden()/notFound() (403/404): in Next.js 16.4.3 either one thrown by a page escapes the server render, the response is an empty <html id="__next_error__"> shell drawn on the client, and the enforced Trusted Types CSP blocks that draw (no 'default' policy without the root layout's head): a blank page. The server still refuses every call the role may not make.

items.raw_text: Publish the region tile host (WP1/WP8) before the pilot and set CARPAL_ADMIN_MAP_STYLE_URL in the console (and the PWA's style URL): without a basemap, staff correcting a pin see the pins on a blank map and must rely on the typed coordinates and the distance.
items.proposal: After the region tile host is published (WP1/WP8, backend/infra), set the PWA map style URL (CARPAL_PWA_MAP_STYLE_URL, deploy env) and the console one (CARPAL_ADMIN_MAP_STYLE_URL). Check the PWA CSP picks up the tile origins and that region config (map.style_url, map.tiles_url) matches. Without it the PWA falls back to the built-in style without a basemap.
known_pwa_context: Region config still points at cdn.carpal.app (backend NI-22, Go-live item in the console handoff notes)
open_questions: Final tile host name and who publishes it.
Should the PWA read the style only from region config and drop the env override?
items.note_2026_11_16: Still infra and owner preparation (backend pilot_prep_checklist_non_code); not part of the backend refinement. Later on 2026-11-16: superseded by PB-10 (owner decision: Neshan instead of a self-hosted tile host).

Reconcile pwa legal:check and the bundled legal texts with the backend texts.

items.proposal: Sign-up shows the terms and privacy texts from policy.current (region, locale) and sends their policy_version; on 409 POLICY_VERSION_OUTDATED reload the text and ask again. After sign-in and on app start read Me.policy_reconsent: a blocking dialog for terms and privacy, a one-time notice for the community guidelines (DQ-02, DQ-17), answered with policy.accept. Render the bodies as Markdown without HTML. Retire CARPAL_PWA_TERMS_VERSION / CARPAL_PWA_PRIVACY_VERSION and reconcile pwa legal:check and the bundled legal pages with the backend texts. Build together with PB-02 (one prompt).
known_pwa_context: pwa legal:check and the bundled legal pages (P13)

items.raw_text: PWA (follow-up S15 + S15b, build once): next to each consent switch and prompt show the consent text from policy.current/{consent_type} and send its policy_version (consents.grant, consents.request_respond, share_history with vehicle_data_policy_version, share_vehicle_context), instead of CARPAL_PWA_PRIVACY_VERSION; on 409 POLICY_VERSION_OUTDATED reload the text. The re-consent prompt also lists Me.policy_reconsent entries of mode consent: confirm with policy.accept (all consents of that type) or withdraw single consents (consent_ids); say that the feature is paused when paused is true. Settings: show reconsent_required, paused and confirmed_policy_version on consent rows.
items.proposal: Next to each consent switch and consent prompt show the text from policy.current/{consent_type} and send its policy_version (consents.grant, consents.request_respond, share_history with vehicle_data_policy_version, share_vehicle_context). The re-consent prompt of PB-01 also lists the Me.policy_reconsent entries of mode consent: confirm with policy.accept or withdraw single consents (consent_ids); say that the feature is paused when paused is true (DQ-19). Settings shows reconsent_required, paused and confirmed_policy_version on the consent rows.
items.owner_note: The final consent texts of the 13 consent types are published together with this item (backend S15b-D1).

items.raw_text: Recommendation R-04: run the console's `pnpm i18n:check` (or its whole `pnpm check`) whenever shared/ changes, and mention the console in shared/i18n/package.json 'description' at the next PWA stage that touches shared/i18n.
items.trigger: the next PWA stage that touches shared/i18n
items.proposal: Mention the admin console (namespaces common and format) in shared/i18n/package.json 'description'. The order of checks is now one command: in backend/, pnpm check:clients (backend S25b: backend contract:check, PWA and console contract:generate, pnpm check in both); run it whenever shared/ or Docs/40 changes.
items.done_part: pnpm check:clients exists (backend S25b, the R-04 root script).

items.raw_text: R-11 (PWA half): the PWA's two integration suites (src/server/bff/bff.int.test.ts, hosted-signin.int.test.ts) build a lite BFF (strict: false) and call /oauth/token and the search directly without a client assertion or DPoP, so they cannot run against the strict backend of `pnpm int:env backend`.
items.proposal: Read CARPAL_STRICT_AUTH and CARPAL_PWA_CLIENT_PRIVATE_JWKS in the two suites as the console's bff.int.test.ts does: strict BFF config with privateKeyJwt for cp-web-consumer and cp-ssr; sign the direct /oauth/token calls (refresh reuse, revoked token) with the client assertion and a DPoP proof, and call the search with a DPoP-bound token. Then `pnpm int:env clients pwa` (in backend/) runs them against the one strict backend; until then `pnpm int:env backend --lite` and `clients --lite`.

items.raw_text: Owner, 2026-11-16: "DQ-24: monthly ODOmeter prompt: please add it, but data entry should be voluntry (user can skip) - add the prompt to PWA (if not there), and add the routing in the backend to receive and record data (in historical sequence)".
items.found_in_pwa: Not there yet. The vehicle header (src/features/garage/vehicle-header.tsx, W-GAR-01) has the inline mileage edit with the "Mileage went down" check and writes vehicles.mileage_add; there is no monthly prompt, no notification route to it and no skip.
items.proposal: C-GARAGE-08 as a sheet that opens from (a) the push or in-app notice vehicle.odometer_prompt (deep link to the vehicle, sheet open) and (b) a garage card shown while Vehicle.odometer_prompt.due is true. The sheet reuses the header's mileage logic (last value and date, numeric field, lower-value check with Fix last entry / Save anyway) and has two actions: Save (vehicles.mileage_add with recorded_at now, or a date the person picks for a reading taken earlier) and "Skip this month" (vehicles.odometer_prompt_skip; no reading written, the card disappears). Answering is voluntary: closing the sheet does nothing, and nothing nags. Add the template text vehicle.odometer_prompt (EN/FA) to the catalog as a consumer template, the notification preference under Reminders, and refresh vehicles.get, vehicles.list and vehicles.mileage_list after Save or Skip. Tests: deep link opens the sheet, Skip calls the operation and hides the card, Save writes a reading, back-dated date accepted, RTL.

items.raw_text: Owner, 2026-11-16: "for maps, I am planning to use a local map provider from www.neshan.org (api documentation is available here: https://platform.neshan.org/docs/)".
items.trigger: after backend S26b.T3 and the owner's Neshan web map key
items.proposal: Neshan basemap in the map pages (search map pane, location pickers): keep MapLibre and load a Neshan style built from the region config (vector basemap day/night by theme, no traffic, no Neshan POI layer), with the web map key from CARPAL_PWA_NESHAN_MAP_KEY attached as the Neshan docs require (transformRequest), never stored in Web Storage. Add the Neshan origins to the page CSP (map-config.ts mapTileOrigins: vts.neshan.org, static.neshan.org; and the RTL text plugin from static.neshan.org or a self-hosted copy), the "© Neshan" attribution and logo as the terms require, the built-in fallback style kept for outages. If the docs allow only Neshan's SDK (mapbox-gl 1.13 fork, stores the key in localStorage), stop and ask: it conflicts with the PWA's CSP and Web Storage rules. Tests: CSP origins, fallback on style failure, RTL labels, attribution visible.
depends_on: Neshan web map key restricted to pwa.carpals.ir
